# SMB Support

`customer_support.model.smb_support` · model · parent `—`

> Small businesses, bought from a pricing page or after one call, on a plan anyone can cancel this afternoon. The defining inversion is that the stakes per contact are high and the revenue per contact is tiny. The person in the ticket is the owner, the payer, the admin and the one currently losing money; "could you ask your IT team to check that" has no referent, and neither does "let me pick this up with your account manager on Monday". . Volume is high against revenue that cannot fund a human on the majority of contacts, so the model only closes if self-service, macros and automated answers carry the mass. Deflection here is not an efficiency programme layered on top of a support org — it is the support org, and every point of it is the margin that pays for the humans who handle what is left. . Entitlement exists but is uniform. It is a plan tier from a price list, not a negotiated schedule, so verification collapses to a lookup and the expensive enterprise work of interpreting a bespoke contract does not exist at all. What exists instead is the plan boundary as an upsell surface that every agent stands on daily. There is likewise no escalation path in either direction: no procurement, no sponsor, no committee — the owner IS the executive and they are already in the thread. When an SMB customer escalates, the channel is a review site, a chargeback or the cancel button, and none of the three route to us. . What an operator carries over wrongly from enterprise or mid-market: investigating properly. Forty minutes of careful diagnosis on an account paying fifty a month is that account's entire year of margin, and a known workaround delivered in four minutes with an article attached is the correct answer rather than a lazy one. The carry-over error in the other direction, imported from self-serve, is treating every deflection as a saving. A retailer locked out of their till at nine on a Saturday is not deflectable, will not file a ticket and wait, and the coverage gap on the day their business actually trades is what ends the account — silently, because nobody in an SMB base writes a churn explanation.


## Characteristics

|  |  |
|---|---|
| requester | the owner or one of a handful of employees; buyer, payer, admin and affected user in the same person, with no internal IT to escalate to |
| typical_resolution_hours | 4 |
| volume_shape | high volume against low revenue per account; sharply peaked at the start of the business day, at month-end billing, and on any pricing or packaging change |
| staffing_model | pooled generalists behind heavy self-service, no tiers and no named owners; specialist pods only for billing and fraud |
| coverage | extended weekday hours, with weekend cover wherever the customer base trades at weekends — a retail or hospitality SMB base has its worst hour on a Saturday and its thinnest staffing at the same time |
| automation_level | very high by necessity — the price point cannot fund a human on the majority of contacts, and the ones that do reach a human are therefore the hard ones by construction |
| buyer | the owner, on a card, from a pricing page or after a single call |
| typical_cycle_days | 7 |
| typical_acv | three to low four figures a year, frequently billed monthly and cancellable in a click without speaking to anyone |
| committee_size | one |
| decision_style | immediate, emotional and reversible; the same person can buy on Tuesday and cancel on Thursday, and will tell a review site before they tell us |
| primary_channels | `chat`, `help_center`, `email`, `phone` |
| notes | Billing is the highest-emotion queue in this branch and it is not a finance concern. A card decline or a failed renewal charge on an SMB account arrives as an existential problem — the business stops — and routing it by ticket type into a back-office queue with a slower service standard is the most reliable way to manufacture a public complaint out of a two-minute fix.  |

## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.knowledge_article`

Requires `findability`, `zero_result_query_count`, `intent_covered`, `locale`


> The article is the first line, not the documentation of a resolution, and the reader is a busy owner on a phone between customers of their own. An article that is correct and unfindable is operationally identical to one that does not exist. `zero_result_query_count` is the branch's best leading indicator of queue volume: every failed search is a ticket that has not been filed yet, and it arrives roughly a day later with a frustrated tone that the ticket record will attribute to the wrong cause.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.entitlement`

Requires `plan`, `entitled_channels`


> Entitlement here is a tier from a price list — uniform, machine-readable, never negotiated — so the expensive part of entitlement_verification (interpreting a bespoke schedule) simply does not exist, and an org importing an enterprise verification procedure is paying for a lookup. What does exist is the plan boundary as an upsell surface, and the judgement call is whether "your plan does not include phone support" is said to a customer whose business is currently stopped.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.requester`

Requires `is_affected_user`, `preferred_channel`, `technical_fluency`


> The requester is the affected user and there is nobody behind them. Every diagnostic step that begins "ask your administrator to" terminates immediately, so fluency is not a nice-to-have on this object — it decides whether the diagnosis can be run at all or whether we have to infer from symptoms. Channel preference is equally load-bearing: this person cannot sit in a chat queue while their shop is open.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.churn_risk`


> Cancellation is self-serve and instantaneous. There is no renewal conversation in which the risk surfaces and no CSM who notices — the support ticket IS the renewal conversation, and it is happening right now, mid-thread. The corollary is unpleasant and true: by the time churn risk is derived from behaviour after the fact, the account has usually already gone, so the only useful reads on this object in this branch are the in-conversation ones.


## Extends `customer_support.obj.core.ticket`

Requires `channel`, `ticket_type`, `requester_ref`


> Ticket type carries urgency that the severity field does not. Billing, access and payout tickets are revenue-stopping for this customer whatever their technical severity, and a queue sorted purely on severity puts them behind genuinely lower-stakes defects every single day.

## Metadata

owner **Customer Support** · updated 2026-08-08 · review **unreviewed** · confidence **provisional**


> Segment branch. Deliberately distinguished from plg_self_serve, which shares its economics and not its stakes: a PLG contact is usually a comprehension failure by someone evaluating, an SMB contact is frequently a business interruption for someone committed. The two branches emphasise similar capabilities for opposite reasons, and an org that merges them will get the deflection strategy right and the coverage strategy badly wrong.
